hypotheses.justification: `hC` follows from `hlog` and `hW` at the given `t`. Write X = 1 + ‖(U.velocity t).toLp‖ + W t * log (exp 1 + tensorNorm 3 (U.velocity t)). (1) `U.gradientNormPath t` is nonnegative: it is defined as `‖finiteField (U.velocity t).derivative‖`, and the library proves `U.gradientNormPath_nonneg t` (OrdinaryEulerGradientControl.lean:416). (2) X ≥ 1 > 0: `tensorNorm 3 _` is a finite sum of norms (OrdinaryH3Norms.lean:28), hence nonnegative, so by monotonicity of log the log term is at least log (exp 1) = 1 ≥ 0; `hW t` gives W t ≥ 0; and the norm term is nonnegative. (3) `hlog t` gives 0 ≤ gradientNormPath t ≤ C * X, so `nonneg_of_mul_nonneg_left` (Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Ring/Unbundled/Basic.lean:344) applied to 0 ≤ C * X and 0 < X yields 0 ≤ C. There is no degenerate case, because `t` is an argument of the theorem, so `Icc 0 T` is nonempty. The new proof first derives `hC` this way at the start and is otherwise unchanged, including the two uses of `mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ... hC`.
